previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis, cirrhosis, and a history of recurrent cholangitis was readmitted for recurrent right upper quadrant abdominal pain and low-grade fever. She had recently completed a course of ertapenem for a prior cholangitis episode. Imaging revealed biliary sludge and a small stone in the gallbladder remnant. An ERCP was performed, which showed no strictures and allowed for removal of sludge from the bile duct. Antibiotics were switched from ertapenem to meropenem for a targeted seven-day course post-procedure. Her symptoms resolved, liver enzymes improved, and she remained afebrile. She was discharged home with plans to continue IV meropenem via her existing PICC line, restart home diuretics, and follow up for lab monitoring and outpatient procedures. Her transplant status remains unchanged.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a very pleasant ___ year old woman with a history 
of sclerosing cholangitis complicated by cirrhosis Child's B, 
MELD 9, ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, and recurrent 
cholangitis who presents with RUQ pain, fever, and malaise.

# RUQ pain, fever, malaise: There was concern again for 
recurrent of cholangitis, particularly with elevated bilirubin, 
her history, and her constellation of symptoms. She has a 
history of MDR cholangitis, most recent episode earlier this 
month and completed a course of antibiotics on ___ with 
meropenem. Differential also included cholecystitis, SBP, 
pancreatitis She was empirically started on meropenem. She was 
afebrile with no leukocytosis, and no growth on any cultures. 
Her RUQ ultrasound did not show enough ascites for a tap, CT 
abdomen did not show any abscesses, did show non specific 
colitis but patient had recent normal colonoscopy. Infectious 
disease team was consulted and felt this was not acute 
cholangitis given lack of supporting data, but given history 
agreed on short 5 day course of meropenem. Given her past 
breakthrough symptoms with doxycycline, rifaximin and 
ciproflacin and leg pain with moxifloxacin, they recommended 
continuing rifaximin for suppression (patient has confirmed 
sulfa and ampicillin allergies-hives), however only noted 
vomiting as a reaction to cefuroxime, no other known 
cephalasporin allergies. Patient was stable and asymptomatic on 
discharge.

# Primary sclerosing cholangitis: Complicated by hepatic 
encephalopathy, ascites, esophageal varices. Child Class B, MELD 
around 9. Currently on the transplant list. We held Lasix and 
spironolactone for now given dry appearance on exam. She was 
continued on home hydroxyzine 50 mg QHS pruritis, Cholestyramine 
4g daily, Ursodiol 300 mg TID, Temazepam 15 mg QHS PRN insomnia, 
Lactulose 15 mg BID PRN constipation, Rifaximin 550 mg BID. She 
is not on nadolol due to prior reported adverse symptoms. 

# H/O esophageal varices: She is not maintained on any beta 
blocker given that she has had an adverse reaction to nadolol 
(elephant sitting on chest, dizziness). Last endoscopy in 
___ was without evidence of varices.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with h/o PSC, recurrent cholangitis, p/w
recurrent RUQ pain  // Please assess for e/o bile duct dilatation. ?Presence
of ascites

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made with CT abdomen and pelvis from ___
and MRCP from ___.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The liver is coarsened and nodular in echotexture. The contour of the
liver is nodular, consistent with cirrhosis.  Three scattered echogenic foci
are again seen right hepatic lobe, possibly reflecting granulomas.  The main
portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. There is mild ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation.  2 stones are noted in
the remnant cystic duct, unchanged from prior exam.  The CBD measures 4 mm.

GALLBLADDER: The patient is status post cholecystectomy.

PANCREAS: Imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits, without
masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic tail
obscured by overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 15.3 cm.

KIDNEYS:  Limited views of the right kidney are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  No acute findings.  No biliary dilatation.  Mild ascites.

2. Cirrhotic liver with splenomegaly and mild ascites.

3.  Re-demonstration of 2 stones in the gallbladder remnant.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with PSC, hx of recurrent cholangitis who
presents with fevers, RUQ pain, leukocytosis.  // rule out hepatic abscess?

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Stationary Acquisition 7.0 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 33.7 mGy (Body) DLP =
16.9 mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 4.5 s, 48.9 cm; CTDIvol = 16.0 mGy (Body) DLP = 783.6
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 800 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CTA abdomen on ___ and MRCP on ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Visualized lung fields are within normal limits. There is no
evidence of pleural or pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: As before, the liver demonstrates findings of cirrhosis such as
left-sided atrophy, atrophy of the right posterior segments and a micronodular
contour.  There is trace hepatic free fluid.  Minimal intrahepatic biliary
ductal dilatation is re- demonstrated and not significantly increased from the
prior examination in ___.  There is no extrahepatic biliary ductal
dilatation.  No focal hepatic fluid collection or focal hepatic lesion is
identified on this single phase examination.  Numerous intra-abdominal varices
are demonstrated.  The gallbladder is surgically absent.

SPLEEN: The spleen is enlarged at 14 cm.  The spleen is normal in attenuation.

PANCREAS: The pancreas shows normal enhancement.  There is no pancreatic duct
dilatation or peripancreatic fat stranding.

ADRENALS: The adrenal glands are unremarkable bilaterally.

URINARY: The kidneys display symmetric nephrograms with no evidence of
hydronephrosis or mass lesion in either kidney.  The ureters are symmetrical
in their course to the bladder.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is within normal limits.  Small bowel loops are
normal in caliber and wall thickness.  There is minimal fluid within the right
pericolic gutter as well as minimal edema involving the ascending colonic wall
which may be due to third spacing or possible inflammation.

LYMPH NODES: There are no pathologically enlarged retroperitoneal or
mesenteric lymph nodes by CT size criteria.

VASCULAR: The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber and demonstrates minimal to
moderate calcified atherosclerosis.

PELVIS: The bladder is within normal limits.  The rectum and sigmoid colon are
within normal limits.  There is no pelvic or inguinal adenopathy.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES: There are no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions seen
in the visualized osseous structures.

IMPRESSION:


1. Mild intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation consistent with a history of
PSC is not significantly increased from ___.  No focal hepatic fluid
collection or focal hepatic lesions are identified on this single phase
examination.
2. Cirrhotic liver with sequela of portal hypertension including varices,
trace perihepatic ascites and splenomegaly.  The patient is status post
cholecystectomy.
3. Minimal free fluid within the right pericolic gutter as well as mild
thickening of the wall of the ascending colon.  This may be related to third
spacing/portal colopathy however colitis should be considered in the
appropriate clinical setting.
